step1_cost_basis.rule: conservative: the larger of the two measured candidate types
step1_cost_basis.why: the 46-candidate production mix was not individually measured; the real F_0 candidate has decaying Chebyshev coefficients and is 1.360x CHEAPER than the protocol's declared dense-random benchmark. Basing a cap on the cheaper candidate is precisely how the previous cap became insufficient.

step2_plus_cusum.why: the aux4 CUSUM cover is byte-identical on this host and is INHERITABLE, but a re-run allowance is budgeted so that an adjudicator may lawfully require a re-run without a second budget failure.

step3_frozen_overhead.why: the benchmark measured contraction only. The frozen model already carries OVERHEAD=1.15 for certificate generation and per-cell setup: K1_total = OVERHEAD*(t_panel*EVALS/3600 + CUSUM). Reused unchanged.

step4_timing_variance.why: measured replicate variance was <=0.44% on CPU and <=3.03% on throughput; 5% covers that band plus host-level jitter across a multi-day run.

step5_retry_resume.why: resume granularity is ONE CELL. An abrupt host loss forfeits at most the in-flight cell of each of the 16 workers. Two such events are budgeted.

step6_assembly_verification.why: aggregate ledger, governed-input manifest, re-hash and audit of all 316 cell records, and the final adjudication pass.

step7_cap.why: clean rounded cap 5.7% above the derived requirement. It binds only in the adversarial candidate case, which is what a cap is for.
